calibration_summary: AHCI 1.3.1 itself defines no calibration loops at the register level — the HBA register file is purely digital and requires no trim. All analog calibration lives one layer below in the SATA PHY: TX de-emphasis level, RX equalization, CDR loop bandwidth, common-mode bias, and OOB envelope detector thresholds are tuned per silicon process / package / SI characterization. Speed Negotiation is the only spec-mandated 'closed-loop' procedure visible to software — the host advertises its highest supported Gen, and the device drops down until both agree.

speed_negotiation_sequence.purpose: Find the highest Gen (1.5 / 3 / 6 Gbps) at which both host and device can reliably communicate over the present cable / connector / backplane SI environment.
speed_negotiation_sequence.control_register: PxSCTL.SPD limits the maximum speed the host advertises (0=no limit / 1=Gen1 / 2=Gen2 / 3=Gen3).
procedure: After OOB completion, host transmits training primitives at its highest supported rate.
If device cannot lock, host drops to the next-lower Gen and retries.
Negotiation is performed by the PHY; AHCI software observes the result via PxSSTS.SPD only.
speed_negotiation_sequence.error_recovery: If too many CRC errors are observed at the negotiated speed (PxSERR.ERR.CRC / DataIntegrity), software may force PxSCTL.SPD to cap a lower speed and re-issue PxSCTL.DET=1 to renegotiate.

phy_calibration_areas_implementation_spe: TX de-emphasis level (typically programmable via vendor PHY config registers — not exposed by AHCI)
RX continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE) + DFE coefficients (vendor PHY tuning)
CDR loop bandwidth + phase-interpolator step size
no_software_visible_calibration_loop: Unlike PCIe (which has spec-defined Phase 1/2/3 receiver equalization at Gen 3+) or UHS-I SD (CMD19 tuning block), AHCI 1.3.1 / SATA do not define a software-visible per-link equalization loop. Once the link reaches L0, no further line-rate calibration is mandated.

devsleep_timer_tuning.PxDEVSLP_DITO_field: Device Sleep Idle Timeout — software-configurable; HBA waits DITO ms idle before asserting DEVSLP (when PxDEVSLP.ADSE=1 + CAP2.SADM=1).
devsleep_timer_tuning.PxDEVSLP_DM_field: DITO Multiplier — extends DITO range to up to 16 × 16368 ms.
devsleep_timer_tuning.PxDEVSLP_MDAT_field: Minimum DevSleep Assertion Time — HBA must hold DEVSLP HIGH at least MDAT ms (nominal 10 ms, min 1 ms) before de-asserting.
devsleep_timer_tuning.PxDEVSLP_DETO_field: DevSleep Exit Timeout — maximum time from DEVSLP de-assertion until device is ready (nominal 20 ms, max 255 ms).

no_card_side_trim: AHCI does not expose any trim / calibration register on the SATA wire. Device-internal NAND / spindle / head calibration is vendor-specific and out of scope.
notes: The only software-visible calibration AHCI defines is Speed Negotiation via PxSCTL.SPD ↔ PxSSTS.SPD and the DevSleep timing envelope via PxDEVSLP DITO / MDAT / DETO fields. Everything else (TX de-emphasis, RX equalization, CDR, OOB thresholds) is vendor-PHY territory.
